output.summary: KEP-1898 proposes hardening kubelet exec endpoints against SSRF by requiring POST for most exec requests and removing command control via URL parameters; it is marked implementable at alpha stage.
output.rationale: SSRF vulnerabilities (CVE-2020-8559, CVE-2018-1002102) become more severe when an attacker can run arbitrary commands via a GET URL parameter. The KEP limits exec via GET, keeping websocket support, and removes URL-parameter command control. The maintainers accepted the breaking changes, with the kubelet API as the target because only kube-apiserver consumes it.

alternatives.why_not: The readme says that more exec-related vulnerabilities are likely in the future, so the risk remains.
The readme calls this probably a non-starter because it drops a supported feature.

alternatives.option: Require the websocket protocol for GET requests (sub-protocol hash approach)
alternatives.why_not: The maintainer said the hash approach provides sufficient protection with minimal changes, and this was preferred over the signed exec token and the in-stream exec options. The exact reason for not selecting it as the final design is not fully stated in the sources.

alternatives.option: Signed exec token request (POST to get signed params, then GET)
alternatives.why_not: The maintainer said it would require managing a signing key.

evidence.quote: Mitigate the potential for privilege escalations via SSRF vulnerabilities by requiring a POST method for most exec requests, and limiting control of the executed command via URL parameters.
In both these cases, the potential of the vulnerability is greatly increased by the ability for an attacker to execute arbitrary commands specified by a URL parameter in a GET request.
Alternative 2 (exec token request) would require managing a signing key and option 3 (make request over the websocket connection) would be a much larger change.
Looks like this is not going to make the code freeze cutoff. /milestone v1.21

I'm clearing the milestone to reflect that this enhancement was not entered into the [tracking sheet](http://bit.ly/k8s121-enhancements) before the enhancements freeze, therefore not opting into the 1.21 release.
